primary_diagnosis_treated: Metabolic syndrome (including hypertension, dyslipidaemia, pre‑diabetes, obesity, CKD stage 4)
nice_guideline_used: CG181 / NG28 (Metabolic syndrome components), NG136 (Hypertension), NG107 (CKD), NG28 (Diabetes), TA775 (SGLT2‑inhibitor in CKD)

medications.duration: Lifelong — review annually and after any dose change
medications.purpose: Essential hypertension and renoprotection in CKD
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG136 recommends ACE‑I as first‑line antihypertensive in CKD

medications.dose: 40 mg once daily in the evening
medications.duration: Lifelong — review lipid profile at 12 weeks then annually
medications.purpose: Dyslipidaemia; reduce cardiovascular risk in CKD/metabolic syndrome
medications.nice_justification: NICE CG181/NG28 advise high‑intensity statin for CKD stage 3‑5 or QRISK ≥10%

medications.duration: Lifelong — review renal function and genital infection risk every 6 months
medications.purpose: Renal protection and modest glucose‑lowering in CKD eGFR 20‑45 mL/min/1.73 m²
medications.nice_justification: NICE TA775/NG28 recommends SGLT2‑i for CKD stage 4 irrespective of diabetes status

medications.dose: 5 mg once daily (titrate to 10 mg if needed)
medications.duration: Lifelong — add only if BP ≥140/90 mmHg after 4 weeks of ACE‑I
medications.purpose: Second‑line antihypertensive to achieve target BP
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG136 recommends CCB as add‑on when ACE‑I alone insufficient

medications.dose: 0.25 mg weekly, titrate to 0.5 mg after 4 weeks (max 1 mg)
medications.duration: Lifelong — review weight, HbA1c and GI tolerance every 6 months
medications.purpose: Weight management and glycaemic control in obesity with pre‑diabetes
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG28 recommends GLP‑1 RA for obesity (BMI ≥30) with pre‑diabetes or early T2DM

interactions_checked.interaction: Additive blood‑pressure lowering may cause symptomatic hypotension, especially early after starting dapagliflozin
interactions_checked.action: Check BP and orthostatic symptoms after 1–2 weeks; consider reducing lisinopril if systolic <110 mmHg

interactions_checked.interaction: Combined ACE‑I and CCB can increase serum potassium
interactions_checked.action: Monitor serum K⁺ and creatinine 2 weeks after adding amlodipine

interactions_checked.interaction: Co‑administration of two statins increases risk of myopathy and rhabdomyolysis
interactions_checked.action: Stop Simvastatin 48 h before starting Atorvastatin; monitor CK at baseline and 12 weeks

interactions_checked.interaction: GLP‑1 RA may delay gastric emptying and reduce absorption of oral statins
interactions_checked.action: Take atorvastatin at least 1 hour before or 2 hours after semaglutide injection

contraindications.reason: eGFR estimated <30 mL/min/1.73 m² (creatinine 3.2 mg/dL) – risk of lactic acidosis
CKD stage 4 – NSAIDs worsen renal function and increase fluid retention
CKD stage 4 – can worsen electrolyte balance and glucose tolerance
contraindications.alternative: Consider low‑dose thiazide only if needed and monitor electrolytes

contraindications.reason: Severe renal impairment (eGFR <30) – risk of prolonged hypoglycaemia
contraindications.alternative: DPP‑4 inhibitor if additional glucose‑lowering needed

assumptions_warnings: Exact eGFR not provided; assumed CKD stage 4 (eGFR ~20‑25 mL/min/1.73 m²) based on serum creatinine 3.2 mg/dL.
Current blood pressure reading not available; assumed not at target (<140/90 mmHg) prompting conditional amlodipine addition.
HbA1c not reported; assumed pre‑diabetes (fasting glucose 5.6‑6.9 mmol/L) per problem list.
QRISK score not calculated; assumed ≥10% given CKD, hypertension, obesity, dyslipidaemia.
Allergy status unknown – verify no hypersensitivity to ACE‑I, statins, SGLT2‑i or GLP‑1 RA before prescribing.
Liver function tests not provided; obtain baseline ALT/AST before initiating atorvastatin or semaglutide.
treatment_summary: Continue lisinopril for hypertension and renal protection, switch low‑dose simvastatin to high‑intensity atorvastatin 40 mg nightly, add dapagliflozin 10 mg daily for CKD renoprotection, consider amlodipine 5 mg if BP remains uncontrolled, and offer semaglutide for weight loss and pre‑diabetes. Avoid metformin, NSAIDs, high‑dose thiazides and sulfonylureas due to CKD. Monitor BP, renal function, electrolytes, lipid profile, CK, and glycaemic parameters as per NICE guidelines.
